subtopics.title: Energy and Infrastructure
subtopics.summary: India's renewable energy progress, the revival of the Mohra hydropower plant and the Dedicated Freight Corridors form this infrastructure block. Renewables make up a large share of non-fossil capacity, and solar is the largest part of the energy mix. The Western and Eastern corridors separate freight traffic from passenger lines.
facts: India ranked 3rd globally in renewable energy capacity, after China and the United States
Total installed non-fossil capacity is 283.46 GW; renewable capacity is 274.68 GW
55.29 GW of non-fossil capacity added in FY 2025-26
Energy mix: Solar 54.7%, Wind 20.4%, Large Hydro 18.7%, Bioenergy 4.3%
India achieved its 50% non-fossil power capacity target under the Paris Agreement, 5 years ahead of 2030
Mohra Power Project is also known as Mahura Power Project and sits on the Jhelum River
Mohra is located at Uri, Baramulla (Jammu and Kashmir) and was commissioned in 1905
Western DFC: 1506 km, from JNPT (Maharashtra) to Dadri (Uttar Pradesh)
Eastern DFC: 1337 km, from Ludhiana (Punjab) to Sonnagar (Bihar)
DFC conceived in 2005, approved by Cabinet in 2008, implemented by DFCCIL

subtopics.title: International Groupings and Peacekeeping
subtopics.summary: This block covers the regional and UN-linked bodies in the booklet. AZEC is a clean-energy platform for Asia, while UNIFIL is a UN force in Lebanon that patrols the Blue Line. ECOSOC and the G7 complete the section, with ECOSOC acting as a UN coordination platform and the G7 working as an informal forum without a treaty.
facts: AZEC was launched in 2023 on Japan's proposal as a regional platform for clean energy transition
AZEC members: Australia, Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Japan, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam
AZEC Plus extends the community to additional partner countries such as ASEAN and India
UNIFIL was created by the UN Security Council in 1978 to verify Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon
Blue Line: UN-demarcated boundary between Lebanon and Israel
UNIFIL mandate: monitor ceasefire, patrol Blue Line, ensure humanitarian access, assist Lebanese Armed Forces
ECOSOC: established 1945, one of 6 principal UN organs, 54 members, headquarters in New York
ECOSOC: 18 members elected each year for a 3-year tenure
India elected unopposed to four ECOSOC subsidiary bodies for 2026-2028, its 18th tenure
G7 is an informal, non-treaty forum with no permanent secretariat; decisions taken by consensus

subtopics.title: Finance, Enforcement and Cyber Cooperation
subtopics.summary: This block links banking liquidity with financial crime and cyber-fraud cooperation. The RBI's VRR auctions injected liquidity for year-end banking stability, while FIU-India and I4C work on financial and cyber frauds. The GlobE Network builds cross-border action against corruption and illicit assets.
facts: RBI announced a 21.25 Lakh Crore liquidity infusion through VRR auctions for year-end banking stability
VRR is a liquidity injection tool under RBI's Liquidity Management Framework for temporary shortages
Banks borrow short-term funds from RBI by providing government securities (G-Secs) as collateral
VRR funds are provided through auction-based repos, with a duration of 7 to 14 days
FIU-India: established 2004, nodal ministry is Ministry of Finance, focus on anti-money laundering
FIU-India collects and analyses suspicious financial transaction reports and shares intelligence
FIU-India and Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre signed an MoU to combat cyber-financial frauds
I4C: established 2018 under Ministry of Home Affairs as central agency for cybercrime coordination
GlobE Network: formally launched 2021, concept from Riyadh Initiative during Saudi Arabia's G20 Presidency (2020)
GlobE operates under the UN Convention Against Corruption and aims to recover illicit assets

subtopics.title: Health, Nutrition and Rankings
subtopics.summary: This block covers nutrition policy, BRICS health cooperation and higher-education rankings. Mission POSHAN 2.0 and a 15-day campaign focus on nutrition for women and children. India's 2026 BRICS Presidency includes a health working group on prevention and mental health, and QS 2026 rankings placed IIM Kozhikode in the global top 100.
facts: 15-day nationwide campaign aims to drive behavioural change and improve nutritional outcomes for women and children
Mission POSHAN 2.0 was launched in 2021 to create an Integrated Nutrition Support System
India holds the 2026 BRICS Presidency and hosted a BRICS Health Working Group meeting in New Delhi
BRICS Mission for Healthy Lifestyles focuses on prevention of non-communicable diseases
BRICS Mental Health and Wellness Initiative aims to strengthen mental healthcare and reduce stigma
Integration of Traditional Medicine includes systems like AYUSH (India)
QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026: IIM Kozhikode entered the Global Top 100
India ranks 4th globally in total institutions ranked and new entries
IIT Delhi leads India in Engineering and Technology in the QS rankings
Indian institutions entered the QS Marketing rankings for the first time

quizzes.title: Energy and Freight Infrastructure MCQs
quizzes.passage:
India's energy and freight networks drew attention in April 2026. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy highlighted the country's progress in renewable energy capacity, policy reforms and the wider energy transition. Solar power forms the largest part of the national energy mix, and India has built up a large stock of non-fossil capacity. The country also reported strong additions to its non-fossil capacity during the last financial year, adding to a broader push towards cleaner power.

Hydropower is also being revived. The Jammu and Kashmir government has moved to restore the Mohra Power Project, a historic plant on the Jhelum River in Uri, Baramulla. The move is meant to boost hydropower capacity at a time when the Indus Waters Treaty faces uncertainty.

Freight infrastructure also reached a milestone. The Ministry of Railways completed the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, which links the Jawaharlal Nehru Port Terminal in Maharashtra with Dadri in Uttar Pradesh. The Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor runs from Ludhiana in Punjab to Sonnagar in Bihar.

questions.q: In which year was the Mohra Power Project commissioned?
questions.explanation: The booklet states the Mohra Power Project was commissioned in 1905.

questions.q: What is the length of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the Western DFC length as 1506 km, from JNPT to Dadri.

questions.q: In which year was the Dedicated Freight Corridor project approved by the Cabinet?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the project was conceived in 2005 and approved by Cabinet in 2008.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor keeps freight traffic apart from passenger lines.
Reason (R): The corridor is a flagship initiative aimed at separating freight traffic from passenger lines.
options: Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the DFC as a flagship initiative aimed at separating freight traffic from passenger lines, which is why A holds.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor   ->   B. 1337 km
II. Western Dedicated Freight Corridor   ->   D. 1506 km
III. Mohra Power Project   ->   A. Commissioned in 1905
IV. Solar share of India's energy mix   ->   C. 54.7 per cent
questions.explanation: The booklet gives 1337 km for the Eastern DFC, 1506 km for the Western DFC, 1905 for Mohra's commissioning and 54.7% for solar.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Mohra Power Project is also known as the Mahura Power Project.
II. The Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor is longer than the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor.
III. Wind accounts for a larger share of India's energy mix than large hydro does.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is in the booklet, II is false because 1337 km is shorter than 1506 km, and III holds as wind is 20.4% against 18.7% for large hydro.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. India achieved its 50 per cent non-fossil power capacity target five years ahead of 2030.
II. India ranks third globally in renewable energy capacity.
III. Bioenergy is the largest contributor to India's energy mix.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are in the booklet, while III is false because solar at 54.7% is the largest share.

questions.q: How much non-fossil capacity did India add in FY 2025-26? (in GW)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that 55.29 GW of non-fossil capacity was added in FY 2025-26.

quizzes.title: International Groupings TITA
quizzes.passage:
International cooperation in April 2026 covered energy, peacekeeping and economic governance. India's External Affairs Minister took part in a meeting of a regional platform that works on clean energy transition and energy security in Asia, where energy market disruptions were discussed. The platform was proposed by Japan and seeks to promote decarbonisation and sustainable energy systems across the region.

India also condemned the killing of Indonesian peacekeepers serving with a United Nations force in Lebanon. That force monitors the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon, patrols the boundary between them, supports humanitarian access for civilians and assists the Lebanese Armed Forces. Its purpose includes verifying the withdrawal of Israeli forces from southern Lebanon.

At the United Nations, India was elected unopposed to four subsidiary bodies of the Economic and Social Council for the period 2026 to 2028. The Council is one of the principal organs of the United Nations and acts as a central platform for global economic, social and environmental issues.

The Group of Seven is an informal forum that works without a treaty and has no permanent secretariat. It brings together advanced economies along with the European Union, and its decisions are taken by consensus. India's External Affairs Minister was invited to the G7 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in France as a partner.

questions.q: In which year was the Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC) launched? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states AZEC was launched in 2023 on Japan's proposal.

questions.q: In which city is the headquarters of the UN Economic and Social Council located?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the ECOSOC headquarters as New York (USA).

questions.q: In which year did the G7 begin as the G6 forum? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the G7 began in 1975 as the G6 to tackle global economic crises.

questions.q: Which country joined the G6 in 1976, turning it into the G7? (country)
questions.explanation: The booklet states Canada joined in 1976, after which the group became the G7.

questions.q: How many member States does the UN Economic and Social Council have? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists ECOSOC membership as 54 States.

questions.q: In which year did the UN Security Council create the UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL)? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says UNIFIL was created by the UN Security Council in 1978.

questions.q: What is the name of the UN-demarcated boundary between Lebanon and Israel that UNIFIL patrols?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Blue Line as the UN-demarcated boundary between Lebanon and Israel that UNIFIL patrols.
